items.question: A dark rim 1.5 mm thick is seen around the heart at end-systole at 24 weeks. What is this?
options: A normal small amount of pericardial fluid
items.explanation: Pericardial fluid of 2 mm or less at end-systole is common in the second and third trimesters and is normal.

items.question: A gap appears in the ventricular septum near the crux in an apical view, with the beam along the septum. What should you do before calling it a defect?
options: Look again with the beam perpendicular to the septum
Measure the gap and report its size
Ignore it; septal defects cannot be seen before birth
items.explanation: With the beam parallel to the septum, drop-out can falsely suggest a defect near the crux; the septum is best seen with the beam perpendicular.

items.question: At 34 weeks the right ventricle looks slightly larger than the left. At 20 weeks the same degree of difference is seen in another fetus. How do the two differ?
options: Mild disproportion can be a third-trimester variant; asymmetry in mid-gestation warrants further examination
The third-trimester finding is the more worrying
items.explanation: Mild disproportion can be a normal variant in the third trimester, but right-left asymmetry in mid-gestation warrants further examination.

items.question: The pulmonary artery looks slightly larger than the aorta. How is this read?
options: A reason for further evaluation in every case
items.explanation: The pulmonary artery is usually slightly larger than the ascending aorta in fetal life. Only a major discrepancy should lead to further evaluation.

items.question: Ectopic beats are occurring after every second normal beat. Is this still within the benign pattern the guideline describes?
options: No: ectopic beats more often than every three to five beats are an indication for further assessment
Yes: all ectopic beats are benign
Yes, provided the four-chamber view is normal
items.explanation: Frequent ectopic episodes, more than every three to five beats, are an indication for further assessment.

items.question: What does the guideline say about an echogenic intracardiac focus and the risk of congenital heart disease?
options: Evidence is insufficient that the risk is significantly above baseline
It is a common indication for fetal echocardiography
items.explanation: Echogenic intracardiac focus is among the factors for which evidence of risk significantly above baseline is insufficient.

items.question: The heart rate rises to 170 for a few seconds during vigorous fetal movement, then settles at 145. How is this read?
options: It can be a normal variant
items.explanation: Mild transient tachycardia (160 to 180) can be a normal variant during fetal movement; persistent tachycardia at 180 or more needs further evaluation.

items.question: On the three-vessel-and-trachea view there is a relatively dark area between the great vessels and the front of the chest. What normal structure appears like this?
items.explanation: The thymus appears as a relatively dark area between the great vessels and the front of the chest.
